claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an fcc matrix.
The as-manufactured alloy exhibits high strength.
The as-manufactured alloy exhibits notable fatigue performance.
Elevated-temperature degradation is governed by the formation and continuity of a protective chromium-rich oxide layer.
Chromium preferentially oxidizes in an oxidizing gas environment.
Preferential chromium oxidation produces an adherent and continuous oxide scale.
A continuous chromium-rich oxide scale passivates the surface and limits further oxidation.
The protective chromium-rich scale helps preserve mechanical integrity during oxidizing exposure.
Under reducing or low-oxygen-partial-pressure conditions, the protective chromium-rich oxide does not form or becomes unstable.
The absence or instability of the protective scale under reducing conditions causes accelerated internal oxidation.
Reducing exposure causes degradation of the fcc matrix.
Oxidizing exposure will produce a stable protective chromium-rich oxide scale.
Mechanical properties will change only modestly under oxidizing exposure.
Reducing exposure will produce more internal oxidation or microstructural damage than oxidizing exposure.
Internal oxidation or microstructural damage under reducing exposure will correlate with greater fatigue degradation.

contradictions.description: The baseline is called a starting-state or as-manufactured baseline, but it is also defined as behavior during oxidizing exposure with expected passivation. An unexposed as-built state and an oxidized/passivated state are distinct baselines.
